title: Model
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. In the first two-dimensional sketch, on the first face, draw the first loop by starting with a line from the point (0.0097, 0.0) to (0.7403, 0.0). Next, draw an arc from (0.7403, 0.0) to (0.7403, 0.0194) with a midpoint at (0.75, 0.0097). Follow this with a line from (0.7403, 0.0194) to (0.0097, 0.0194), and complete the loop with an arc from (0.0097, 0.0194) to (0.0097, 0.0) with a midpoint at (0.0, 0.0097). For the second loop, start with a line from (0.0097, 0.0015) to (0.7403, 0.0015), then draw an arc from (0.7403, 0.0015) to (0.7403, 0.0179) with a midpoint at (0.7485, 0.0097). Continue with a line from (0.7403, 0.0179) to (0.0097, 0.0179), and finish the loop with an arc from (0.0097, 0.0179) to (0.0097, 0.0015) with a midpoint at (0.0015, 0.0097). Scale the entire sketch by a factor of 0.75. Transform the scaled sketch into three dimensions by rotating it with Euler angles set to zero and translating it with a vector also set to zero. Extrude the sketch 0.0095 units along the normal direction to create a new solid body. The final dimensions of the model are a length of 0.75 units, a width of 0.01938369781312127 units, and a height of 0.009468190854870774 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch for the cross-section
r = r.moveTo(0.0097, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.7403, 0.0) \
     .threePointArc((0.75, 0.0097), (0.7403, 0.0194)) \
     .lineTo(0.0097, 0.0194) \
     .threePointArc((0.0, 0.0097), (0.0097, 0.0)) \
     .close()

# Define the inner loop for the cross-section
r = r.moveTo(0.0097, 0.0015) \
     .lineTo(0.7403, 0.0015) \
     .threePointArc((0.7485, 0.0097), (0.7403, 0.0179)) \
     .lineTo(0.0097, 0.0179) \
     .threePointArc((0.0015, 0.0097), (0.0097, 0.0015)) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create the 3D object
r = r.extrude(0.0095)

# Scale the sketch (if necessary)
# Note: The sketch scale is applied to the sketch before extrusion, but in this case, it is already scaled.
# If you need to scale the final object, you can use the `scale` method.
# r = r.scale(0.75)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

    .lineTo(0.0005, 0.0095).threePointArc((0.0000, 0.0050), (0.0005, 0.0005)) \
    .close().extrude(0.75)

    .lineTo(0.01865, 0.00075).threePointArc((0.0194, 0.00475), (0.01865, 0.00875)) \
    .lineTo(0.00075, 0.00875).threePointArc((0.0000, 0.00475), (0.00075, 0.00075)) \
    .close().extrude(0.0005)

# Subtract Part 2 from Part 1
